function.name: weather_forecast_get
function.description: Retrieve the current weather forecast for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location you want to retrieve the weather for.

hour.description: The hour of the day in 24-hour format (optional). If not provided, the current hour will be used. Default: 24

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time data, so I can’t tell you the exact current time in New York City right now.
message.reasoning: The user asks "紐約市現在是幾點？" which means "What time is it now in New York City?" We need to provide the current time. But we don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we can't fetch real-time. According to policy, we should not fabricate. We could use the weather_forecast_get function with location "New York City" and hour=0? That returns forecast, but not time. There's no function to get time. So we should respond that we cannot determine the exact current time. Maybe we can give an approximate based on UTC offset. But better to say we don't have real-time capability.
